div.head: Leis Wl 36
div.ab: Si home enpuissuned altre, seit occis u permanablement eissilled.
De ueneficio. Si quis alterum ueneno occiderit, aut occidatur aut in exilium perpetuum agatur.
Si home enpuissuned altre, seit occis u permanablement eissilled.
36. Wenn jemand einen anderen vergiftet, werde er getödtet oder dauernd verbannt.
36. If someone poisons another, he shall be killed or permanently banished.
If a man poisons another, he shall be slain or sent into permanent exile.
div.note: Some of Liebermann’s notes here are cut off in the gutter of the scan used, and are still to be completed.
Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 268–269 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text and German translation added from Gesetze I p. 514, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

note.seg: Vgl. Gl Gift 5. 6. [Um 970 versucht Klerus den Bischof Æthelwold von Winchester zu vergiften; Ælfric Vita Æthelwoldi.] Ob Spur echten Gesetzes Wilhelms? An den Röm. Wortlaut klingt in L nur veneficio an, was Zufall sein kann. In Lex Rom. Visigoth. Paul. V 25 sent. 13 fehlt veneficiis

Cf. Gl Gift 5. 6. [About 970 clergy attempt to poison Bishop Æthelwold of Winchester; Ælfric Vita Æthelwoldi.] A trace of a genuine law of William’s? In L only veneficio echoes the Roman wording, which may be chance. In Lex Rom. Visigoth. Paul. V 25 sent. 13 veneficiis is missing
